# GLASS SUPPLY AGREEMENT

This Glass Supply Agreement (this "**Agreement**") is entered into as of February 1, 2024 by and between **Meideis Glass Fabrication Co.**, a Pennsylvania corporation with its principal office at 2200 Furnace Street, Allentown, Pennsylvania 18103 ("**Supplier**"), and **Besouth Facade Systems, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation with its principal office at 715 Harborline Drive, Wilmington, Delaware 19801 ("**Buyer**"). Supplier and Buyer are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. Supplier fabricates insulated, laminated and tempered architectural glass products.

B. Buyer designs, fabricates and installs unitized and stick-built curtainwall and facade systems for commercial construction projects.

C. Buyer wishes to purchase, and Supplier wishes to supply, architectural glass products on the terms of this Agreement and the Statements of Work issued under it.

The Parties therefore agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 **Defined Terms.** In this Agreement:

"**Affiliate**" means, as to any person, any other person that now or hereafter directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with that person. In this definition, "control" means ownership of more than 50% of the voting equity of a person or the power to direct its management and policies, whether by contract or otherwise.

"**Amendment**" means a written amendment to this Agreement signed by both Parties under Section 18.3.

"**Change of Control**" means, as to Buyer, any transaction or series of related transactions in which (a) any person or group of persons acting together acquires, directly or indirectly, more than 50% of the voting equity of Buyer or of any direct or indirect parent of Buyer; (b) Buyer or any direct or indirect parent of Buyer merges or consolidates with another person and the equity holders of Buyer or that parent immediately before the transaction hold less than 50% of the voting equity of the surviving entity immediately after it; or (c) Buyer sells all or substantially all of its assets.

"**Confidential Information**" has the meaning given in Section 12.1.

"**Delivery Point**" means the project site, Buyer facility or other location stated in the applicable Purchase Order.

"**Effective Date**" means the date first written above.

"**Products**" means the architectural glass products listed in Exhibit A, as updated by the Parties in writing or by a Statement of Work.

"**Purchase Order**" means a written order for Products that Buyer issues under this Agreement and a Statement of Work.

"**Specifications**" means the technical requirements for Products in Exhibit A and in the applicable Statement of Work, including referenced ASTM standards, project drawings and approved shop drawings.

"**Statement of Work**" means a project-specific statement of work signed by both Parties that references this Agreement.

"**Term**" means the Initial Term together with any extension under Section 2.2.

1.2 **Interpretation.** Headings are for convenience only. "Including" means "including without limitation." References to Sections and Exhibits are to sections of and exhibits to this Agreement.

## 2. TERM

2.1 **Initial Term.** This Agreement takes effect on February 1, 2024 (the Supply Agreement Effective Date) and continues for an initial term of three years from the Supply Agreement Effective Date (the "**Initial Term**"), unless terminated earlier under Section 15 or Section 16.3.

2.2 **Extension.** The Parties may extend the Term by mutual written agreement signed before the Initial Term expires.

2.3 **Effect on Statements of Work.** Each Statement of Work in effect on expiry or termination of this Agreement continues under its own terms until completion of the project it covers, and this Agreement continues to govern that Statement of Work until then.

## 3. SUPPLY COMMITMENT

3.1 **Exclusive Purchase.** During the Term, Buyer shall, and shall cause its Affiliates to, purchase from Supplier all of its requirements for architectural glass products throughout North America, including insulated glass units, laminated glass, heat-strengthened and fully tempered glass, and coated and spandrel glass, whether for curtainwall, storefront, window wall or other facade applications. Buyer and its Affiliates shall not purchase these products from any other source during the Term.

3.2 **Supply Obligation.** Supplier shall accept and fill Purchase Orders that conform to this Agreement and the applicable Statement of Work, subject to the lead times in Section 5.2.

3.3 **Forecasts.** Buyer shall give Supplier a rolling non-binding six-month forecast of anticipated Product requirements by the tenth day of each calendar quarter.

## 4. STATEMENTS OF WORK AND PURCHASE ORDERS

4.1 **Statements of Work.** The Parties will set out project-specific requirements, including Specifications, quantities, pricing adjustments, delivery schedules and project contacts, in a Statement of Work. Each Statement of Work forms part of this Agreement.

4.2 **Purchase Orders.** Buyer shall order Products by issuing Purchase Orders that identify the applicable Statement of Work, Products, quantities, Delivery Point and requested delivery dates. Supplier shall accept or reject each Purchase Order in writing within five business days of receipt. Supplier may reject a Purchase Order only if it does not conform to this Agreement or the applicable Statement of Work.

4.3 **Conflicting Terms.** Pre-printed or standard terms on any Purchase Order, acknowledgement, invoice or other business form are of no effect.

## 5. DELIVERY

5.1 **Delivery Terms.** Supplier shall deliver Products FCA Supplier's facility (Incoterms 2020), packed on Supplier's returnable racks, to the carrier Buyer designates. If a Statement of Work requires delivery to the Delivery Point, Supplier shall arrange freight, and Buyer shall reimburse freight at cost.

5.2 **Lead Times.** Unless a Statement

of Work states otherwise, Supplier shall deliver standard insulated glass units within six weeks, and laminated or custom-coated units within ten weeks, after it accepts the Purchase Order.

5.3 **Late Delivery.** Supplier shall notify Buyer promptly of any anticipated delay. If Supplier fails to deliver by the confirmed delivery date for reasons other than Force Majeure or Buyer's act or omission, Supplier shall, at Buyer's election, expedite shipment at its own cost.

5.4 **Racks.** Buyer shall return Supplier's racks in good condition within 60 days after delivery, failing which Supplier may invoice Buyer the replacement cost stated in Exhibit B.

## 6. TITLE AND RISK OF LOSS

Title and risk of loss pass to Buyer on delivery of Products to the carrier under Section 5.1, or, where Supplier arranges freight to the Delivery Point, on unloading at the Delivery Point.

## 7. PRICING AND PAYMENT

7.1 **Prices.** Buyer shall pay the prices set out in Exhibit B, as adjusted by any Statement of Work for project-specific Products.

7.2 **Price Adjustments.** Prices are fixed for the first 12 months of the Initial Term. Thereafter, Supplier may adjust prices once per contract year on 60 days' written notice, by no more than the percentage change in the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Producer Price Index for flat glass (PPI series WPU1311) over the previous 12 months.

7.3 **Invoicing.** Supplier shall invoice on shipment. Undisputed invoices are due within 45 days of receipt. Buyer shall notify Supplier in writing of any disputed amount, with reasons, within 15 days of receipt of the invoice, and the Parties shall resolve the dispute under Section 17.

7.4 **Late Payment.** Undisputed amounts not paid when due bear interest at 1% per month or the highest lawful rate, whichever is lower.

7.5 **Taxes.** Prices exclude sales, use and similar taxes, which Buyer shall pay unless it provides a valid exemption certificate.

## 8. QUALITY AND INSPECTION

8.1 **Quality System.** Supplier shall maintain a quality management system for Product fabrication. Its insulated glass units must be certified under the IGCC/IGMA certification program, and its laminated glass must comply with ANSI Z97.1 and 16 CFR 1201 where applicable.

8.2 **Inspection.** Buyer shall inspect Products within 10 business days after delivery and shall notify Supplier in writing of any visible nonconformity or shipping damage within that period. Acceptance does not waive Buyer's rights under Section 9 for latent defects.

8.3 **Rejection.** Supplier shall replace rejected Products at its cost within the lead times in Section 5.2, or within a shorter period agreed in writing where the project schedule requires it.

## 9. WARRANTIES

9.1 **Product Warranty.** Supplier warrants that Products will (a) conform to the Specifications; (b) be free from defects in materials and workmanship; and (c) be free of liens and encumbrances on delivery.

9.2 **Seal Warranty.** Supplier further warrants that insulated glass units will be free from seal failure, material obstruction of vision from film formation or dust, and internal moisture for ten years after delivery. Supplier warrants that laminated glass will be free from delamination for five years after delivery.

9.3 **General Warranty Period.** Except as stated in Section 9.2, the warranties in Section 9.1 apply for 24 months after delivery.

9.4 **Remedies.** For any Product that breaches a warranty, Supplier shall, at its option, repair or replace it, and shall reimburse Buyer's reasonable documented costs of removal and reinstallation, up to the amount stated in Section 11.2.

9.5 **Disclaimer.** EXCEPT AS STATED IN THIS SECTION 9, SUPPLIER MAKES NO OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

## 10. INDEMNIFICATION

10.1 **By Supplier.** Supplier shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Buyer and its Affiliates, and their officers, directors and employees, from third-party claims for bodily injury, death or damage to tangible property caused by defective Products or by the negligence or willful misconduct of Supplier, and from claims that Products infringe a third party's patent, trademark or copyright.

10.2 **By Buyer.** Buyer shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Supplier and its officers, directors and employees from third-party claims for bodily injury, death or damage to tangible property caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of Buyer in handling, glazing or installing Products.

10.3 **Procedure.** The indemnified Party shall notify the indemnifying Party of the claim promptly, shall allow it sole control of the defense and settlement (except that no settlement may impose liability on the indemnified Party without its consent), and shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's cost.

## 11. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

11.1 **Exclusion.** Except for liability under Section 10 or Section 12, or for gross negligence or willful misconduct, neither Party is liable to the other for indirect, incidental, consequential, special or punitive damages, including lost profits.

11.2 **Cap.** Except for liability under Section 10 or Section 12, or for gross negligence or willful misconduct, each Party's total liability under a Statement of Work is limited to the total amounts paid and payable under that Statement of Work.

## 12. CONFIDENTIALITY

12.1 **Definition.** "**Confidential Information**" means non-public information that one Party discloses to the other under this Agreement and that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential, including pricing, Specifications, shop drawings and project information.

12.2 **Obligations.** The receiving Party shall use Confidential Information only to perform this Agreement and shall not disclose it except to its and its Affiliates' employees, advisers and subcontractors who need to know it and are bound by obligati

ons of confidentiality at least as protective as this Section 12.

12.3 **Exceptions.** This Section 12 does not apply to information that is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving Party, was lawfully known to the receiving Party before disclosure, is independently developed, or is required to be disclosed by law, provided the receiving Party gives prompt notice where lawful.

12.4 **Duration.** The obligations in this Section 12 survive for three years after the Term ends.

## 13. INSURANCE

13.1 **Supplier Coverage.** Supplier shall maintain throughout the Term, with insurers rated A- VII or better by A.M. Best:
(a) commercial general liability insurance, including products-completed operations, of at least $2,000,000 per occurrence and $4,000,000 aggregate;
(b) umbrella liability insurance of at least $5,000,000;
(c) automobile liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 combined single limit; and
(d) workers' compensation insurance at statutory limits and employer's liability insurance of at least $1,000,000.

13.2 **Certificates.** Supplier shall name Buyer and its Affiliates as additional insureds on the policies in Sections 13.1(a) and 13.1(b), and shall deliver certificates of insurance to Buyer on the Effective Date and on each policy renewal.

## 14. FORCE MAJEURE

Neither Party is liable for failure or delay in performance (other than payment obligations) caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including fire, flood, epidemic, war, governmental action, labor disputes not involving its own workforce, and failure of float glass supply from primary manufacturers ("**Force Majeure**"). The affected Party shall give prompt notice and use reasonable efforts to resume performance. If a Force Majeure event continues for more than 90 days, either Party may terminate the affected Statement of Work on written notice.

## 15. TERMINATION

15.1 **For Breach.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work on written notice if the other Party materially breaches it and fails to cure the breach within 30 days after receiving written notice describing it.

15.2 **Insolvency.** Either Party may terminate this Agreement on written notice if the other Party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or becomes subject to any bankruptcy or receivership proceeding that is not dismissed within 60 days.

15.3 **Effect.** On termination, Buyer shall pay for all Products delivered and for work in process under accepted Purchase Orders that Supplier cannot reasonably mitigate. Sections 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 17 and 18 survive termination or expiry.

## 16. ASSIGNMENT

16.1 **General.** Neither Party may assign or transfer this Agreement or any Statement of Work, in whole or in part, by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other Party. Any purported assignment in breach of this Section 16 is void.

16.2 **Change of Control.** Any Change of Control of Buyer, including a Change of Control occurring at the level of any direct or indirect parent of Buyer, is deemed an assignment of this Agreement by Buyer and requires Supplier's prior written consent under Section 16.1. Buyer shall notify Supplier in writing of any proposed Change of Control at least 30 days before it is completed.

16.3 **Termination Right.** If a Change of Control of Buyer occurs without Supplier's prior written consent, Supplier may terminate this Agreement and any or all Statements of Work on 30 days' written notice to Buyer, given at any time within 12 months after Supplier learns of the Change of Control.

16.4 **Successors.** Subject to this Section 16, this Agreement binds and benefits the Parties and their permitted successors and assigns.

## 17. DISPUTE RESOLUTION

17.1 **Escalation.** The Parties shall first try to resolve any dispute under this Agreement by referring it to their respective senior executives, who shall meet within 15 days after either Party's written request.

17.2 **Courts.** If the dispute is not resolved within 30 days after that request, either Party may bring proceedings in the state or federal courts located in New Castle County, Delaware. Each Party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of those courts.

17.3 **Injunctive Relief.** Nothing in this Section 17 prevents a Party from seeking interim injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction.

## 18. GENERAL

18.1 **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier or by email with confirmation copy by courier, to the addresses below or to another address a Party designates by notice:

To Supplier: Meideis Glass Fabrication Co., 2200 Furnace Street, Allentown, Pennsylvania 18103, Attention: President

To Buyer: Besouth Facade Systems, Inc., 715 Harborline Drive, Wilmington, Delaware 19801, Attention: Chief Executive Officer

18.2 **Order of Precedence.** If there is a conflict among the transaction documents, they prevail in this order: Amendments, then the Supply Agreement, then any Statement of Work.

18.3 **Amendment.** This Agreement may be amended only by a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both Parties.

18.4 **Waiver.** No failure or delay in exercising a right operates as a waiver of it.

18.5 **Severability.** If any provision is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force, and the invalid provision is to be replaced by a valid provision that comes closest to the Parties' intent.

18.6 **Governing Law.** This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.

18.7 **Independent Contractors.** The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture or agency relationship.

18.8 **Counterparts.** This Agreement may be signed in

# STATEMENT OF WORK NO. 1: CALLOWAY PIER TOWER

This Statement of Work No. 1 (this "**SOW**") is entered into as of March 18, 2024 by and between **Meideis Glass Fabrication Co.** ("**Supplier**") and **Besouth Facade Systems, Inc.** ("**Buyer**") under the Glass Supply Agreement between Supplier and Buyer dated as of February 1, 2024 (the "**Agreement**"). This SOW is a Statement of Work under the Agreement and forms part of it under Section 4.1 of the Agreement. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this SOW have the meanings given in the Agreement.

## 1. PROJECT

1.1 **Project.** Calloway Pier Tower, a 31-story mixed-use residential and office tower at 1400 Calloway Pier Road, Baltimore, Maryland 21231 (the "**Project**").

1.2 **Project Parties.**

| Role | Party |
|---|---|
| Owner | Calloway Pier Owner LLC |
| General Contractor | Tidewater Hallcroft Builders, Inc. |
| Architect of Record | Norquist Lavelle Architects, P.C. |
| Curtainwall Subcontractor | Besouth Facade Systems, Inc. |
| Glass Fabricator | Meideis Glass Fabrication Co. |

1.3 **Buyer's Scope.** Buyer holds the subcontract for design, fabrication and installation of the unitized curtainwall system for the Project's tower levels 3 through 31 and the podium storefront at levels 1 and 2. Supplier will fabricate and supply the glass described in Section 3 for incorporation into Buyer's units.

## 2. EXCLUSIVITY AND PROJECT COMMITMENT

2.1 **Exclusivity.** Supplier will be Buyer's exclusive source of insulated glass units for the Calloway Pier Tower project, Baltimore, Maryland. Buyer will not purchase insulated glass units for the Project from any other source while this SOW is in effect.

2.2 **Estimated Quantities.** Buyer estimates its Project requirements at approximately 186,000 sq. ft. of insulated glass units, broken down in Section 3.2. These quantities are estimates for planning purposes. Buyer's purchase commitment is set by the Purchase Orders it issues under this SOW.

2.3 **Duration.** This SOW takes effect on the date above and continues until Supplier has delivered all Products ordered under it and the warranty periods in Section 7 have run, or until it is terminated earlier under the Agreement.

## 3. PRODUCTS AND SPECIFICATIONS

3.1 **Products.** The Products under this SOW are the following items from Exhibit A to the Agreement, in the makeups described below:

| Type | Exhibit A Item | Makeup | Location |
|---|---|---|---|
| IGU-1 | A-1 / A-5 | 1" overall dual-pane: 1/4" heat-strengthened low-E (#2 surface) / 1/2" argon-filled airspace / 1/4" heat-strengthened clear | Tower vision, levels 3–31 |
| IGU-2 | A-1 / A-3 / A-5 | 1-5/16" overall dual-pane: 1/4" heat-strengthened low-E (#2 surface) / 1/2" airspace / 9/16" laminated heat-strengthened clear, 0.060" PVB | Podium storefront, levels 1–2 |
| IGU-3 | A-1 / A-6 | 1" overall dual-pane: 1/4" heat-strengthened low-E (#2 surface) / 1/2" airspace / 1/4" heat-strengthened with ceramic frit (#4 surface) | Tower spandrel, levels 3–31 |
| IGU-4 | A-2 / A-5 | Triple-pane, 1-3/4" overall, low-E #2 and #5 surfaces, argon fill at 90% minimum | Mechanical penthouse, level 31 acoustic zone |

3.2 **Estimated Quantities by Type.**

| Type | Estimated Area (sq. ft.) | Estimated Unit Count |
|---|---|---|
| IGU-1 | 128,500 | 4,620 |
| IGU-2 | 14,200 | 410 |
| IGU-3 | 38,900 | 1,540 |
| IGU-4 | 4,400 | 150 |
| **Total** | **186,000** | **6,720** |

3.3 **Specifications.** Products must conform to the following, which together with Exhibit A to the Agreement are the Specifications for this SOW:

(a) Project Specification Section 08 44 13 (Glazed Aluminum Curtain Walls) and Section 08 81 00 (Glass Glazing), Issue for Construction set dated January 26, 2024;

(b) Buyer's approved shop drawings and glass schedule, as revised and approved by the Architect of Record from time to time;

(c) low-E coating: Solarban 70 or approved equal, with performance values within the tolerances stated in Specification Section 08 81 00;

(d) spacer: warm-edge stainless steel, black finish; secondary seal: structural silicone compatible with Buyer's structural glazing sealant, with compatibility and adhesion test results delivered before first production; and

(e) labeling: each unit to bear a permanent IGCC/IGMA certification label and a removable label showing the Project mark number from Buyer's glass schedule.

3.4 **Mock-Up.** Before production, Supplier will supply glass for Buyer's performance mock-up within six weeks after Buyer's Purchase Order for mock-up glass. Production will not begin until the Architect of Record approves the mock-up and visual samples.

## 4. PRICING

4.1 **Prices.** Prices for Products under this SOW are the base prices in Exhibit B to the Agreement, adjusted as follows:

| Type | Price (USD per sq. ft.) | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| IGU-1 | $27.75 | A-1 base $24.50 + A-5 low-E upcharge $3.25 |
| IGU-2 | $46.10 | A-1 base $24.50 + A-5 low-E upcharge $3.25 + laminated lite $18.35 (Project volume rate) |
| IGU-3 | $33.40 | A-1 base $24.50 + A-5 low-E upcharge $3.25 + frit lite $5.65 |
| IGU-4 | $45.25 | A-2 base $38.75 + two low-E surfaces at $3.25 each |

4.2 **Oversize Units.** Units over 50 sq. ft. carry a surcharge of $4.10 per sq. ft. on the whole unit area. Units over 85 sq. ft. or over 144 inches on either dimension will be priced by written quote before Buyer issues the Purchase Order.

4.3 **Mock-Up Glass.** Mock-up glass is priced at the rates in Section 4.1 plus a one-time setup charge of $3,500.

4.4 **Price Adjustment.** Prices under this SOW are subject to adjustment only as provided in Section 7.2 of the Agreement.

4.5 **Freight.** Supplier will arrange freight to the Delivery Point under Section 5.1 of the Agreement, and Buyer will reimburse freight at cost.

## 5. DELIVERY

5.1 **Delivery Point.** Buyer's unitizing facility at 2950 Broening Highway, Baltimore, Maryland 21224, unless a Purchase Order designates the Project site for direct-to-s

calloway_pier_tower_statement_of_work.md, page 2 of 2:
ite storefront glass.

5.2 **Release Schedule.** Buyer will release Purchase Orders by floor sequence according to the Project schedule it delivers to Supplier, as updated monthly. Buyer will release each tower floor sequence at least eight weeks before the required delivery date.

5.3 **Lead Times.** The lead times in Section 5.2 of the Agreement apply, except that IGU-2 and IGU-4 units have a lead time of twelve weeks after Supplier accepts the Purchase Order.

5.4 **Delivery Sequencing.** Supplier will deliver units in mark-number sequence according to Buyer's floor release. Each rack must carry a packing list showing Project mark numbers, unit sizes and type designations.

5.5 **Breakage and Remakes.** Supplier will give priority to remakes for broken or rejected units. It will ship remakes for nonconforming units within three weeks after Buyer's notice under Section 8.2 of the Agreement.

## 6. QUALITY

6.1 **Testing.** Supplier will deliver to Buyer, before first production shipment, the following:

(a) current IGCC/IGMA certification for each unit construction;

(b) ASTM E2190 test reports; and

(c) structural silicone adhesion and compatibility reports referred to in Section 3.3(d).

6.2 **Visual Quality.** Visual quality will be assessed under ASTM C1036 and C1048 at the viewing distances and conditions stated in Specification Section 08 81 00.

6.3 **Site Access.** Supplier will make a technical representative available on request for up to four Project site or unitizing facility visits during production, at no charge.

## 7. WARRANTY

The warranties in Section 9 of the Agreement apply to Products under this SOW, including the ten-year insulated glass seal warranty and the five-year laminated glass delamination warranty in Section 9.2 of the Agreement. On Buyer's request, Supplier will issue a Project-specific warranty certificate in favor of the Owner on the same terms, for inclusion in Buyer's close-out submittals.

## 8. PROJECT CONTACTS

| | Supplier | Buyer |
|---|---|---|
| Project Manager | Daniel Ostrowski, (610) 555-0182, dostrowski@meideisglass.com | Renata Kluge, (302) 555-0147, rkluge@besouthfacade.com |
| Technical / Quality | Lena Harwick, (610) 555-0195, lharwick@meideisglass.com | Marcus Teague, (302) 555-0163, mteague@besouthfacade.com |
| Accounts | ar@meideisglass.com | ap@besouthfacade.com |

Either Party may change its contacts by email notice to the other Party's Project Manager. Formal notices must be given under Section 18.1 of the Agreement.

## 9. GENERAL

9.1 **Incorporation.** The Agreement governs this SOW. Each Purchase Order Buyer issues for the Project must reference "SOW No. 1 – Calloway Pier Tower."

9.2 **Changes.** Changes to the Products, Specifications or quantities that arise from Architect-approved revisions will be documented by revised glass schedule and, where pricing is affected, by written change order signed by both Project Managers.

9.3 **Counterparts.** This SOW may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature.

# AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO GLASS SUPPLY AGREEMENT

This Amendment No. 1 (this "**Amendment**") is entered into as of June 15, 2026 by and between **Meideis Glass Fabrication Co.**, a Pennsylvania corporation ("**Supplier**"), and **Besouth Facade Systems, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation ("**Buyer**"). It amends the Glass Supply Agreement between Supplier and Buyer dated as of February 1, 2024 (the "**Agreement**"). Supplier and Buyer are each a "**Party**" and together the "**Parties**."

## RECITALS

A. The Parties entered into the Agreement for the supply of architectural glass products by Supplier to Buyer, and entered into Statement of Work No. 1 – Calloway Pier Tower dated as of March 18, 2024 under it.

B. Under Section 2.1 of the Agreement, the Initial Term continues for three years from the Supply Agreement Effective Date of February 1, 2024.

C. The Parties wish to provide for renewal of the Agreement after the Initial Term and to set pricing for any renewal period. Under Section 18.3 of the Agreement, the Agreement may be amended by a written instrument signed by authorized representatives of both Parties.

The Parties therefore agree as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

1.1 **Defined Terms.** Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Amendment have the meanings given in the Agreement.

1.2 **New Definition.** Section 1.1 of the Agreement is amended by adding the following definition in alphabetical order:

"**Renewal Term**" has the meaning given in Section 2.2."

1.3 **Term.** The definition of "Term" in Section 1.1 of the Agreement is deleted and replaced with the following:

"**Term**" means the Initial Term together with each Renewal Term and any extension under Section 2.4."

1.4 **Amendment as Amendment.** This Amendment is an "Amendment" for the purposes of the Agreement.

## 2. RENEWAL

Section 2.2 of the Agreement is deleted and replaced with the following Sections 2.2, 2.3 and 2.4, and existing Section 2.3 of the Agreement (Effect on Statements of Work) is renumbered as Section 2.5:

"2.2 **Renewal.** On expiry of the Initial Term, this Agreement will automatically renew for successive renewal terms of 24 months each (each, a "**Renewal Term**"), unless either Party gives the other Party written notice of non-renewal at least 180 days before expiry of the then-current term.

# PARENT GUARANTY

This Parent Guaranty (this "**Guaranty**") is made as of October 5, 2026 by **Besouth Holdings LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company with its principal office at 715 Harborline Drive, Wilmington, Delaware 19801 (the "**Guarantor**"), in favor of **Meideis Glass Fabrication Co.**, a Pennsylvania corporation with its principal office at 2200 Furnace Street, Allentown, Pennsylvania 18103 (the "**Supplier**").

## RECITALS

A. The Supplier and **Besouth Facade Systems, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation (the "**Buyer**"), are parties to the Glass Supply Agreement dated as of February 1, 2024. That agreement was amended by Amendment No. 1 dated as of June 15, 2026 (the "**Amendment**"). In this Guaranty, the Glass Supply Agreement as amended by the Amendment and as further amended from time to time is the "**Supply Agreement**."

B. The Buyer and the Supplier have entered into Statement of Work No. 1 – Calloway Pier Tower dated as of March 18, 2024 under the Supply Agreement. They may enter into further Statements of Work under it.

C. Under Section 2.1 of the Supply Agreement, the Initial Term runs for three years from the Supply Agreement Effective Date of February 1, 2024. Under Section 2.2 of the Supply Agreement, as amended by the Amendment, the Supply Agreement will renew for a Renewal Term of 24 months beginning February 1, 2027.

D. The Guarantor directly or indirectly owns all of the outstanding equity of the Buyer. It will benefit from the Supplier's continued supply of Products to the Buyer during the Renewal Term.

E. As a condition of continuing to extend trade credit to the Buyer during the Renewal Term, the Supplier has requested that the Guarantor give this Guaranty.

The Guarantor therefore agrees as follows:

## 1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

1.1 **Defined Terms.** Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Guaranty have the meanings given in the Supply Agreement.

1.2 **Guaranteed Obligations.** "**Guaranteed Obligations**" means all payment obligations of the Buyer to the Supplier under the Supply Agreement, each Statement of Work and each Purchase Order accepted under them, whether now existing or arising later and whether due or not yet due. These include:

(a) the price of Products delivered;

(b) freight reimbursements;

(c) rack replacement charges under Section 5.4 of the Supply Agreement;

(d) interest on late payments under Section 7.4 of the Supply Agreement; and

(e) amounts payable on termination under Section 15.3 of the Supply Agreement.

1.3 **Interpretation.** Headings are for convenience only. "Including" means "including without limitation." References to Sections are to sections of this Guaranty unless stated otherwise.

## 2. GUARANTY

2.1 **Guaranty of Payment.** Subject to Section 3, the Guarantor absolutely, unconditionally and irrevocably guarantees to the Supplier the full and punctual payment of the Guaranteed Obligations when due. This is a guaranty of payment and not of collection.

2.2 **Payment on Demand.** If the Buyer fails to pay any Guaranteed Obligation when due, and that amount remains unpaid for 10 business days after the Supplier gives the Buyer written notice of the failure, the Guarantor shall pay that amount to the Supplier within 15 business days after the Supplier's written demand. Each demand must:

(a) identify the unpaid invoices or other amounts;

(b) state the amount demanded; and

(c) attach copies of the relevant invoices.

2.3 **No Performance Guaranty.** This Guaranty covers payment obligations only. The Guarantor does not guarantee the Buyer's performance of any non-monetary obligation under the Supply Agreement.

## 3. MAXIMUM LIABILITY

The Guarantor's total aggregate liability under this Guaranty is limited to $4,500,000, plus the Supplier's reasonable costs of enforcement recoverable under Section 10.2. Payments by the Guarantor under this Guaranty reduce the amount available under this Section 3. Payments by the Buyer do not reduce that amount.

## 4. DEFENSES

4.1 **Defenses of the Buyer.** The Guarantor may assert any defense, set-off or counterclaim that the Buyer could assert against the Supplier regarding a Guaranteed Obligation, including a good-faith invoice dispute raised under Section 7.3 of the Supply Agreement. The Guarantor may not assert a defense based on the Buyer's insolvency, bankruptcy or lack of capacity.

4.2 **Waivers.** To the extent permitted by law, the Guarantor waives:

(a) presentment, protest and notice of dishonor;

(b) notice of acceptance of this Guaranty; and

(c) any requirement that the Supplier first proceed against the Buyer or any other person or security before making demand on the Guarantor, other than the notice to the Buyer required under Section 2.2.

4.3 **Changes to the Supply Agreement.** The Guarantor's obligations are not released or reduced by any of the following:

(a) any amendment, extension or renewal of the Supply Agreement or any Statement of Work, including any Renewal Term;

(b) any price adjustment under Section 7.2 or Section 7.6 of the Supply Agreement; or

(c) any waiver or indulgence the Supplier grants to the Buyer.

Section 3 continues to limit the Guarantor's liability in each case.

## 5. REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

The Guarantor represents and warrants to the Supplier, as of the date of this Guaranty, that:

(a) it is a limited liability company duly formed, validly existing and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware;

(b) it has the power and authority to execute, deliver and perform this Guaranty, and has taken all limited liability company action necessary to authorize it;

(c) this Guaranty is its legal, valid and binding obligation, enforceable in accordance with its terms, subject to bankruptcy, insolvency and similar laws affecting creditors' rights generally and to general principles of equity;

(d) the execution, delivery and performance of this Guaranty do not violate its certificate of forma

## 6. SUBROGATION

Until the Guaranteed Obligations then due have been paid in full, the Guarantor shall not exercise any right of subrogation, reimbursement or contribution against the Buyer arising from payments under this Guaranty.

## 7. REINSTATEMENT

This Guaranty is reinstated if any payment of a Guaranteed Obligation is rescinded or must be returned by the Supplier on the insolvency, bankruptcy or reorganization of the Buyer. Reinstatement applies to the extent of the payment so rescinded or returned.

## 8. CONTINUING GUARANTY; CHANGE IN OWNERSHIP

8.1 **Continuing Guaranty.** This is a continuing guaranty. It remains in effect until the later of:

(a) expiry or termination of the Supply Agreement; and

(b) completion of each Statement of Work then in effect under Section 2.5 of the Supply Agreement.

After that date, it continues only for Guaranteed Obligations that arose before that date and remain unpaid.

8.2 **Change of Control of the Guarantor.** The Guarantor may undergo a change of control, including a sale of all or a majority of its equity to a third party. A change of control of the Guarantor does not release, reduce or otherwise affect the Guarantor's obligations under this Guaranty. This Guaranty continues to bind the Guarantor after any change of control. The Guarantor shall give the Supplier written notice of any change of control of the Guarantor within 10 business days after it is completed.

8.3 **Change in Ownership of the Buyer.** If the Guarantor ceases to own, directly or indirectly, a majority of the equity of the Buyer, this Guaranty continues for Guaranteed Obligations arising before that event. The Guarantor may then terminate this Guaranty for Guaranteed Obligations arising after that event by written notice to the Supplier.

## 9. NOTICES

10.2 **Costs.** The Guarantor shall reimburse the Supplier's reasonable documented legal costs of enforcing this Guaranty against the Guarantor, if the Supplier prevails.

10.3 **Amendment and Waiver.** This Guaranty may be amended or waived only by a written instrument signed by the Guarantor and the Supplier. No failure or delay in exercising a right operates as a waiver of it.

10.4 **Severability.** If any provision of this Guaranty is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force.

10.5 **Governing Law.** This Guaranty is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.

10.6 **Jurisdiction.** The Guarantor submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state or federal courts located in New Castle County, Delaware for any proceeding arising out of this Guaranty.

10.7 **Counterparts.** This Guaranty may be signed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together form one instrument.
